answer: Retrospective funding redirection, or "saffron" ledger for short: every payment an identity sends or receives gets a small delayed scoring pass. If a cluster of identities routes value around a ring, their later payouts get a ripple of dilution against the shared pool, so gains from the ring shrink as it grows. A plume of early payouts may still slip through, but the attacker must keep each identity funded and aboveminimum for weeks, costing real capital per node.
